content: तारा .²1 A star or planet in general; हंसश्रेणीषु तारासु <ls>R. 4. 19</ls>; <ls>Bh. 1. 15</ls>. .²2 A fixed star; <ls>Y. 3. 172</ls>; <ls>R. 6. 22</ls>. .²3 The pupil of the eye, the eye-ball; कान्तामन्तःप्रमोदादभिसरति मदभ्रान्ततारश्चकोरः <ls>Māl. 9. 30</ls>; विस्मयस्मेरतारैः <ls n="Māl.">1. 28</ls>; <ls>Ku. 3. 47</ls>. .²4 A pearl. .²5 (in Sāṅkhya <ab>Phil.</ab>) One of the 8 Siddhis. .²6 (in music) <ab>N.</ab> of a Rāga of six notes. .²7 A kind of perfume. .²8 .³({%a%}) <ab>N.</ab> of the wife of Vāli, king of the monkeys, and mother of Aṅgada. She in vain tried to dissuade her husband Vāli from fighting with Rāma and Sugrīva, and married Sugrīva after Vāli had been killed by Rāma. .³({%b%}) <ab>N.</ab> of the wife of Bṛhaspati, the preceptor of the gods. She was on one occasion carried off by Soma (the moon) who refused to deliver her up to her husband when demanded. A fierce contest then ensued, and Brahmā had at last to compel Soma to restore her to her husband. Tārā gave birth to a son named Budha who became the ancestor of the Lunar race of kings (see <ls>Bhāg. 9. 14</ls>). .³({%c%}) <ab>N.</ab> of the wife of Hariśchandra and mother of Rohidāsa (also called Tārāmatī). .³({%d%}) <ab>N.</ab> of a Buddha goddess. .³({%e%}) <ab>N.</ab> of a Śakti; Jaina.
